q: Describe the front panel data network interface layout of the FortiGate 6000F series, including interface types, port ranges, and default speeds. Also list the management/HA/console interfaces on the front panel.
kp: Twenty-four 1/10/25GigE SFP28 data interfaces (ports 1-24), default speed 10Gbps
Four 40/100GigE QSFP28 data interfaces (ports 25-28), default speed 40Gbps
Two front panel 1/10GigE SFP+ HA interfaces (HA1, HA2)
Two 10/100/1000BASE-T out-of-band management interfaces (MGMT1, MGMT2) plus one 1/10GigE SFP+ MGMT3 management interface
One RJ-45 RS-232 serial console and one USB connector

q: How are FortiGate 6000F data interfaces grouped for speed changes, and what happens when you change the speed of a single port? How are ports 25-28 different? Give the CLI command to set a port group to 25Gbps.
kp: Ports 1-20 are divided into groups of four (1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16, 17-20); port21-24 also form a group
All interfaces in a group operate at the same speed; changing the speed of one interface changes the speeds of all interfaces in that group
Ports 25-28 are NOT part of an interface group; each can be set independently
CLI: config system interface / edit portN / set speed 25000full

q: Explain the FortiGate 6000F data plane architecture: what are FPCs, how many does each model include, what do the NP6 and CP9 processors do, and how is traffic distributed to the FPCs?
kp: FortiGate 6000F models include a management board (MBD) and internal Fortinet Processor Cards (FPCs) containing NP6 and CP9 processors
FortiGate 6500F includes ten FPCs; FortiGate 6300F includes six FPCs
Two DP3 load balancers use session-aware load balancing to distribute sessions from front panel interfaces (port1-port28) to the FPCs across a 3.2Tbps integrated switch fabric
NP6 provides fastpath acceleration offloading sessions from the FPC CPU and can handle IPsec VPN encryption/decryption
CP9 accelerates resource-intensive security processes such as SSL VPN, Antivirus, Application Control, and IPS

q: Which FortiGate 6000F models are listed in the 7.6.8 admin guide, and what are the key facts about 6000F HA clustering (interfaces, cluster size, log disks)?
kp: Models: FortiGate 6500F(-DC), 6501F(-DC), 6300F(-DC), 6301F(-DC), 6001F(-DC) - all have the same front/back panel configuration; differences are processing capacity
HA uses the HA1 and HA2 1/10GigE SFP+ interfaces for heartbeat, session sync, and management between two FortiGate-6000s; default speed 10Gbps (1Gbps not recommended)
A FortiGate-6000 HA cluster consists of two (and only two) FortiGate-6000s of the same model
FortiGate 6001F, 6501F, and 6301F include two internal 1 TByte log disks in a RAID-1 configuration

q: Describe the FortiGate 7000E architecture: what modules make up a 7000E product, which chassis slots do they occupy, and how do you install two different FIMs?
kp: A 7000E product = chassis (e.g. 7040E) plus interface modules (FIMs) in slots 1 and 2 and processor modules (FPMs) in slots 3 and up
FIMs provide network connections and session-aware load balancing to the FPMs; example: a 7040E chassis comes with two FIMs (slots 1-2) and two FPMs (slots 3-4)
Interface modules always go in slots 1 and 2; processor modules in slots 3 and up
If the product includes two different FIMs, install the module with the lower model number in slot 1 and the higher model number in slot 2 (e.g. FIM-7901E in slot 1, FIM-7904E in slot 2)

q: How do you manage and upgrade a FortiGate 7000E (which module do you log into, how is configuration synchronized), and how is the product licensed/registered?
kp: You log into the primary FIM in slot 1 (via its management IP) to view status and make configuration changes
The same FortiOS firmware build and configuration runs on each FIM and FPM; changes made on the primary FIM are synchronized to all FIMs and FPMs
Firmware upgrade: log into the primary FIM and upgrade as for any FortiGate; all FIMs and FPMs in the chassis upgrade in one step; traffic briefly interrupts, so upgrade during quiet time
The entire package (chassis + FIMs + FPMs) is licensed and configured as a single product under the chassis serial number, which is used for registration and support

q: Compare the FortiGate 7121F and 7081F chassis (FIM/FPM slot layout), and what processors do the 7000F FPMs include and what are they for?
kp: FortiGate 7121F: two FIMs in slots 1-2 and up to ten FPMs in slots 3-12
FortiGate 7081F: two FIMs in slots 1-2 and up to six FPMs in slots 3-8
FIMs provide data network connections and NP7-accelerated session-aware load balancing
FPMs include NP7 processors (offload data processing from the CPU), CP9 processors (accelerate resource-intensive security processes), and additional data network interfaces

q: How do you connect to and upgrade a FortiGate 7000F, and how is FortiGate 7000F typically deployed in HA including uninterruptible upgrade behavior?
kp: Connect via the MGMT interface IP; by default the MGMT1 interface IP of the FIM in slot 1 is 192.168.1.99
Configuration is made from the FIM in slot 1 and synchronized to the other FIM and all FPMs; all FIMs/FPMs run the same firmware and configuration
Firmware upgrade of all FIMs and FPMs happens in one step and briefly interrupts traffic (quiet-time recommended)

Typically deployed as two chassis in an FGCP active-passive cluster; managed by logging into a MGMT interface (logs you into the primary chassis); if upgrade-mode is set to uninterruptible, the cluster updates firmware in both chassis without interrupting data traffic

q: Per the FG-1000F Series QuickStart Guide, what models does it cover, what are the default management IP and credentials, and what initial setup options are offered?
kp: Covers FG-1000F and FG-1001F
Default MGMT IP is 192.168.1.99; username admin; password left blank
Setup options: set up locally (GUI over Ethernet or CLI over console port) or connect using forticloud.com

For static IP configuration use 192.168.1.1 with subnet mask 255.255.255.0 on the management computer; register the device at support.fortinet.com for FortiGuard updates, cloud management, firmware upgrades, support, warranty

q: Which FortiGate models are covered by each of the four hardware documents in the FortiOS 7.6.8 hardware corpus, and what model gaps exist in that set?
kp: FortiGate 6000F admin guide: 6500F/6501F/6300F/6301F/6001F (+ -DC variants)
FortiGate 7000E admin guide: 7060E, 7040E, 7030E (+ FIMs such as FIM-7901E)
FortiGate 7000F admin guide: 7121F, 7081F (+ FIM-7941F)
FG-1000F Series QSG: FG-1000F and FG-1001F
No separate 7.6.8 admin guides for 2000F/4000F/10000F (or a 6000E) in this document set - a documented model gap
